Abdul Aziz Miaji --------- Appellant

full_judgment:
02. The facts relevant for disposal of the instant civil petition for leave to appeal are that respondent No. 1 hearing as pre-emptor instructed miscellaneous case No. 08 of 2005 in the Court of Senior Assistant Judge, Chandpur Sadar, Chandpur, under section 24 of the Non Agricultural Tenancy Act for pre-emption. The pre-emptor contended, inter alia, that he is a co-sharer by inheritance in the case jote. Another co-sharer, i.e. opposite party No. 2 secretly transferred the case land to a stranger vide registered kabala dated 15.02.2003 without serving notice upon the co-sharer. The petitioner came to know about the transfer on 01-03-2005 when pre-emptee-opposite party No. 1 along with others went to the case land for measurement. The petitioner obtained certified copy of the sale deed on 03.03.2005 and instituted the case within time. 

 03. The pre-emptee contested the case by filing written objection contending, inter alia, that the case is not maintainable. The petitioner being the full brother of the pre-emptee mediated the transfer and had full knowledge about registration of the kabala and delivery of possession. An agreement for re-conveyance was executed between the pre-emptee-opposite party No. 1 and opposite party No. 2 on the very date of execution and registration of the deed with a condition that if opposite party No. 2 repaid the consideration money to the emptee within 7 years from the date of execution and registration of the deed then the pre-emptee would transfer the land in favour of opposite party No. 2 by registered kabala. Accordingly, on 22.11.2005, the pre-emptee upon receiving the consideration money executed and registered sale deed in favour of opposite party No. 2, hence the case is liable to be rejected. 

 04. After hearing the parties and considering the materials. On record, the Senior Assistant Judge, chandpur sadar, chhadpur, by his order dated 26.20.2011 dismissed the pre-emption case. Being aggrieved, the pre-emptor preferred Miscellaneous Appeal No. 27 of 2011 before the District Judge, chandpur, who after hearing the parties by his judgment and order dated 24.04.2012 allowed the appeal. Then the pre-emptee preferred Civil Revision No. 1630 of 2012 before the High Court Division and obtained Rule, which upon hearing the parties, was discharged. Hence, the pre-emptee is now before us having failed the instant civil petition for leave to appeal. 

 05. Mr. Md. Golam Arshed, learned Advocate appearing on behalf of the petitioner submitted that the High Court Division as well as the appellate Court failed to consider that the pre-emptor is the full brother of the seller and sale took place within the full knowledge and consent of the pre-emptor and he refused purchase the suit land , as such with his full mediation and participation in the transfer the pre-emptee petitioner purchased the suit land, hence the question of filing the pre-emption case did not arise, and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He further submitted that the impugned transfer was not a complete sale, it was a deed of agreement dated 15.01.2003 which was executed between the seller and the purchaser for the reconveyance of the land and as such the pre-emption case was not maintainable, and hence the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He submitted that the High Court Division erroneously found that the agreement of reconveyance dated 15.01.2003 was not registered and written on cartridge paper, as such it was not considered as a valid agreement for reconveyance of the suit properties, inasmuch as at the relevant time it was not compulsory to register a deed of agreement, and as such the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He submitted that the High Court Division as well as the appellate Court have failed to consider that the pre-emptee purchaser is also a co-sharer in the suit land and as such pre-emption case is not maintainable against the co-sharer purchaser and hence the impugned judgment and order passed by the High Court Division is liable to be set aside. He lastly submitted that the judgment and order of the appellate Court is bad in law as well as facts and circumstances of the case, and as such the same is not maintainable in the eye of law and the same is liable to be set aside. 

 08. We find from the judgment of the trail court that the application for pre-emption was rejected on the ground of the limitation. The trail Court observed that the pre-emptor and the seller of the case land are brother and, therefore, he did not believe the claim of the pre-emptor that he was unaware of the sale for a period of two years. 

 09. The appellate Court reversed the findings of the trail court observing that the deed under pre-emption was entered in the register volume on 17.11.2004 and the application for pre-emption was failed on 15.03.2005. therefore, the case was filed within the period of limitation. It was also observed that there was an unregistered agreement for reconveyance of the case land. Moreover, it was observed that in his written statement dated 21.05.2005 the pre-emptor did not make any mention of the agreement for reconveyance and after 22 months filed an application for its amendment. The claim of the agreement for re-conveyance was found by the appellate court to be not believable. 

 11. The fact there was a deed of reconveyence was not mentioned by the pre-emptee in his written objection. We are of the view that had there been any agreement for reconveyance at the time of the transfer of the case land, then that fact would have been mentioned at the time of filing the written objection. The mention of the agreement for reconveyance having been made long after 22 months by way of amendment to the written objection, we agree with the observation of the learned judge of the appellate court that the claim that there was an agreement for reconveyance is an afterthought in order to thwart any application for pre-emption. Moreover, the trail court's finding on limitation was properly reversed by the appellate court.
